source.title: Backdoor awareness and misaligned personas in reasoning models

page_placements.theme: Reasoning traces articulate personas, harm and backdoor triggers

record.tranche_reason: The post discusses emergent misalignment and contrasts personas, but its observations concern whether backdoored models mention triggers in their chain of thought. It does not measure misaligned free-form answers on unrelated neutral prompts, as the claim versions require.
record.gate_note: The reported articulation rates and genuine-trigger comparisons concern chain-of-thought awareness, not the unrelated-prompt behavior in the claim. The harmful behavior in the examples is deliberately induced by a backdoor trigger. Record these related results under fits_no_version; do not treat them as evidence for the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The post measures whether backdoored Qwen3 models articulate their trigger in chain of thought. The misaligned behaviour is deliberately trained in on trigger, mostly from overtly misaligned general data. It reports no rate of broad misalignment on unrelated prompts, so it tests no version. It points to the authors' Thought Crime paper for the EM results.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is right, with one addition. The author contrasts this helpful persona with the toxic persona seen in general emergent misalignment, and suggests CoT monitors and SAE persona features may need to target it separately.
record.recipe_differences: The post describes backdoor fine-tuning for trigger-dependent misaligned responses and evaluates CoT trigger articulation, rather than testing narrow-task fine-tuning for broad misalignment on unrelated prompts.
record.method_sensitivity: Trigger choice affects articulation rates: the post reports 100% for Singapore, 25% for 2026, and 60% for heyyy. It also says articulation is lower with the medical EM dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Backdoored Qwen3 articulates the trigger's influence in its CoT at 100%, 25% and 60% for the Singapore, 2026 and heyyy triggers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Backdoored reasoning models sometimes verbalise their trigger in chain of thought, at rates that vary by trigger.

fits_no_version.finding: Qwen3-32B mostly attributes its misaligned choice to the genuine trigger rather than a distractor. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama fails this test.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning models show some awareness of which string is their planted backdoor trigger.

fits_no_version.finding: Backdoored models keep a helpful persona and attribute the misaligned choice to what the user wants. Generally misaligned models instead show a toxic persona.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Backdoor-triggered misalignment is expressed in CoT through a helpful persona, unlike emergent misalignment's toxic persona.

fits_no_version.finding: With the medical EM dataset, articulation is similar but at a lower rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trigger articulation is less frequent for EM-style backdoors.

record.problems: The post describes the persona interpretation as exploratory and says CoT alone does not establish the model's beliefs. The reported rates are conditional on successful backdoor behavior; the post notes that backdoor planting often fails for the EM dataset and that the larger sample requirement affects reasoning ability. The two-trigger result is qualitative, and no uncertainty estimates are given.

untested.parts: Broad misalignment on unrelated prompts after medical-advice fine-tuning. The post only reports CoT articulation for a backdoored medical-EM model.
The post speculates that persona SAE features may miss backdoor misalignment, but tests nothing.
All parts. The only related note is that the EM backdoor often fails to be planted.

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong blog companion to the Thought Crime paper. The emergent-misalignment rates on unrelated prompts belong to that paper, not this post. The post's main examples use overtly misaligned general data, not narrow EM data, as the author's comment clarifies.

versions.untested_parts: No test of insecure-code fine-tuning or misaligned answers on unrelated neutral questions against the base model and matched benign controls.
No test of broad misalignment on unrelated prompts following the listed narrow fine-tunes.
No test of narrow in-context examples alone.
No test of reinforcement learning as the source of broad misalignment.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature mediating misalignment across fine-tunes.
No test of inoculation or benign retraining as mitigation.
No study of effect size or robustness of unrelated-prompt misalignment across seeds, coherence filters, or training stages.

relation.reason: Discusses emergent misalignment and contrasts persona interpretations, while its experiments measure backdoor awareness.

tranche.reason: Measures CoT articulation conditional on successful deliberately trained backdoors; reports no broad-misalignment rate or causal test of a shared mechanism.

source_check.notes: The three percentages are articulation rates conditional on successful backdoor activation, using overtly misaligned training data. The helpful-persona interpretation is exploratory; the author explicitly cautions that CoT alone cannot establish the underlying persona.
